avis.titre: Not Harsh, Not Hype — Just Really Good Retinol Skincare
avis.texte: At 52, post-menopausal, with dry skin that can also lean sensitive, I’ve become very selective about retinol products. Retinol can be one of the best ingredients for smoother texture, refined pores, firmer-looking skin, and overall skin quality—but it can also be one of the easiest ways to irritate mature skin if the formula is poorly balanced. That is why I appreciate products like this. This is not a miracle serum that will erase years of aging in a week. It is something better: a well-formulated maintenance retinol serum that helps keep skin on track, looking smoother, healthier, and more refined with consistent use. The first thing I noticed was how pleasant the formula feels. It has a smooth, lightweight serum texture that spreads easily and absorbs well without feeling greasy, sticky, or heavy. Some retinol products feel medicinal or harsh from the moment they touch the skin. This one feels modern and user-friendly, which makes it much easier to stay consistent. And consistency is where retinol wins. What I appreciate most is that this feels like a formula designed for real-world use. Instead of being so aggressive that you use it twice and quit, it feels balanced enough to incorporate into a long-term routine. With regular use, I noticed my skin looking smoother, fresher, and more refined. Texture improved, overall tone looked better, and the skin had that healthier “well-maintained” appearance that often matters more than dramatic short-term claims. I also like the in

Omgggg love this so much! I see results after 1 week of use. I feel like it shaved off some aging. I see it in the overall balancing of my skin and around my eyes! Just turned 35! I got the medicube collagen spray and was not a fan. This is much better!

I'm a skincare nerd and I enjoy taking a close look at the ingredient list. The Medicube Retinol Boosting Serum has some interesting and practical ingredients such as encapsulated retinol (“retinol-some”), retinal, peptides, antioxidants, plus barrier supporting goodies like ceramide NP, cholesterol, squalane, and beta-glucan. The actives are buffered a bit by the soothing/support ingreidents which theoretically should help lessen the potential irritation of retinol. At first glance, 1.9% retinol-some seems to be a high concentration. But that % is not retinol concentration, it's the retinol complex/liposomal delivery system concentration. The encapsulation system helps improve stability and reduce irritation compared with free retinol formulas. Most prescription retinol starts at 0.5% to give you a better idea, this probably has much less than that. I wish the actual retinol % concentration was disclosed as that is a big factor in figuring out if this is a good fit, depending on whether you are new to retinol or a seasoned actives user. It's important to note that the serum also includes numerous botanical extracts and ferments, including spearmint extract, which is a potential irritant for some sensitive skin folks. Not really sure why it's included in this along with citric acid and ferulic acid which increase irritation risk. Usually vit c is used in routines separately due to them both having irritation potential. I'm happy at least that it doesn't have added fragrance.
